title: She saw more (Mekhilta, Shirata 3)
hookLine: a servant girl at the sea saw more than the prophet Ezekiel
tomorrow: "i will glorify Him." okay, but how, exactly?

cards: At a magic show the adults watch the magician's hands. A kid near the front shouts: it's in his other sleeve! Sometimes the one nobody asked sees it first.
When the sea split and Israel crossed, they sang: "This is my God, and I will glorify Him." The Mekhilta, a midrash on Exodus, stops on one small word: this.

teach.b: You only say this about something you can point at.
So the Mekhilta says: a servant girl at the sea saw what Isaiah and Ezekiel never saw. Ezekiel wrote, "the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God." Visions, through an opened sky.
The girl at the sea didn't need a vision. She pointed. This.
Notice who the midrash picked. Not a priest, not a scholar, not a prophet.

teach.h: NOT A PROPHET. A SERVANT GIRL.
teach.b: A servant girl, someone nobody in Egypt asked for an opinion.
Now the week, back as one picture. An owner who answers. Stones joined.
A ladder you climb anyway. A thorn bush with fire in it. A name made of deeds.
A coal on the lips. Each one is about who gets seen and who gets sent, and none of them are the obvious choices. The servant girl at the sea belongs on that list.

how: The Song at the Sea (Exodus 15) is read in synagogues on the Sabbath of Song and on the seventh day of Passover, and is part of the daily morning prayers.

o: the one nobody asked saw clearest
a servant who told Pharaoh his dream
a prophet's vision written in a scroll

games.q: who saw what — tap the pairs.
p: said about what you can point at

s: in the Mekhilta, only prophets truly saw God at the sea
a servant girl saw what Isaiah and Ezekiel didn't.
the midrash builds on the small word this
you say this about what you can point at.
in Jewish stories, only scholars and clergy see clearly
the Mekhilta picks a servant girl as its example.

games.q: your youngest cousin notices something about grandpa that every adult missed. the adults wave it off. what does the Mekhilta say?
o: listen: at the sea a servant girl saw more than prophets.
kids exaggerate; trust the grown-ups who know more.
only listen if a teacher or rabbi agrees with her.
games.why: the Mekhilta's example is a servant girl: she saw what Ezekiel saw only in visions.

practice: Look out a window, or around the room, and find one thing you've walked past again and again without seeing. Look at it for the whole sit, as if no one had ever described it to you.
Trust what your own eyes find there, and if a word comes, let it be a quiet this.

wordCard.voice: She saw more: the Mekhilta on the song at the sea. A servant girl, pointing, saw what prophets saw only in visions.

orig.note: Hebrew: this is my God (Exodus 15:2); the Mekhilta hears pointing in this.

carryVoice: For the road: she saw more, with her own eyes. Two weeks of midrash, read.
